Overview

AIMS360 Design System 16/11/2026

A living reference for AIMS360's foundations and components: the same colors, typography, and Bootstrap components already used across the product's features. This guide keeps growing — every new component gets documented here with the same format: description, live demo, and code snippet.

What changed in this version · UI Audit (approved 13/11/2026)

Every decision of the October 2026 UI Audit (Jira epic ERPDEV-4551) is now part of the Design System, so Runway and this guide say the same thing. The interactive tracker with Live · Design System · Proposal lives in prototypes/feature-ui-audit/.

Values & behaviors

From the Brand Personality section of the Brand Book — what AIMS360 holds dear and how that shows up in every interaction.

Brand story & voice

Founded in 1984 in Los Angeles' Garment District, AIMS360 grew out of an earlier venture called Mr. Software into today's leading fashion ERP. Fashion is what brings people together — it tells the world who we are — and AIMS360 exists to give that industry the technology to move faster, connect further, and stay firmly in control.

"We see it all. Because we've seen it all."

Wordmark personality: Modern. Welcoming. Fashionable.

Semantic tokens in use

The names already used across the product's header, menu, and features, and which scale step they map to.

Information is sky blue. --status-info is #0A6FB8 (one shade darker than the original #7ABEFF, which measured 1.97:1 and couldn't be read). It always comes with the ⓘ icon and is reserved for informational content.

Text colors · three only

Everything people read is black. Supporting text uses the same black, slightly lighter, so it still reads as black. Gray appears only on disabled items, so gray always means "not available". Hierarchy comes from typeface and size, never from a gray tone.

Typography

Two typefaces: Poppins for titles, buttons, tabs and menu items; Segoe UI (with its fallback stack) for labels, values, placeholders, table cells and messages. Load Poppins once in the app shell (400 · 500 · 600 · 700). Segoe UI can't be self-hosted (Microsoft license), so Mac uses the fallback stack.

Text rules · one rule per element type

One question decides the casing: is it a name or a sentence? Names (labels, buttons, columns, tabs, titles) capitalize every word. Sentences (help, errors, messages, examples) capitalize only the first word. Fixed terms keep their usual spelling (Login, Email, UPC, QuickBooks), and data is shown exactly as stored.

Mobile considerations

Type gets one step smaller on phones to save vertical space, except text inside fields, which grows to 16px.

Motion

Short, quiet transitions that show what changed and where it came from: the selected option slides instead of jumping, a menu drops in instead of popping. Three speeds for everything, and nothing moves when the person asks their system to reduce motion.

Iconography

The SVG icon library already built for the product's header, menu, and feedback components. All use currentColor or ship as full-color assets, so they inherit context cleanly. Copy the code or download each as a standalone .svg.

Navigation icons

Action icons

The icons for toolbars, action buttons and menu rows. Every component in this Design System takes its icon from this set: use these, don’t draw new ones. Pick & Scan, Pack & Ship, Edit, Settings and Fix Issue are the approved versions; Calendar, alignment and list icons approved on 11/18/2026.

Status & UI icons

Two weights for two contexts: the outline/duotone set for modals (larger, tinted background) and the filled set for toasters (compact, solid fill). See the Modals and Toasters pages for both in use.

Buttons

Four variants by emphasis (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Text) in 3 sizes, plus icon buttons. Every type has the same five states: default, hover, focus (keyboard only), pressed and disabled. Primary actions that wait for the server also show Loading. Hover darkens a button; it never lightens the label.

Focus is for keyboard users: it only appears with Tab, never on a mouse click. It looks like hover on purpose and adds the ring, so a keyboard user always knows which button Enter will press. Try it: click anywhere on this page and press Tab.

Icon buttons, with tooltip

36 × 36, radius 8, the same five states as the secondary button. The tooltip is the button's name: it opens on hover and on keyboard focus, with a 5px arrow pointing at its button, so in a row of six icon buttons there is no doubt which one it names. Hover or Tab through the buttons below.

Mobile considerations

Touch-sized buttons and how a group of buttons lays out on a phone, depending on how many there are.

Phone < 576pxTablet 576–991pxDesktop ≥ 992px

Inputs

One field for text, single select, multi select and date: 1.5px #321FDB border, radius 10, height 38. The client asked for no gray on interactive elements, and the indigo border measures 8.92:1 (the old #ADA6F2 was 2.21:1). Errors turn the border red so they are easy to find when scanning a form.

Toggle switch

A checkbox styled as a track and thumb — used for binary on/off settings, like "Only Show Unread" in the notifications panel.

Combobox

A searchable, single-select dropdown for long lists — pairs a code with a label per row, highlights the current selection, and shows an empty state when nothing matches.

Color label picker

The 12-color palette used to tag a row or a pick ticket — 2 rows of 6, with a "no color" option (checkmark on white) always in the first row.

Mobile considerations

Fields go full width, 44px tall, with 16px text so iOS doesn’t zoom the page.

Phone < 576pxTablet 576–991pxDesktop ≥ 992px

Forms

How fields are put together into a form: one row per field (label · dots · field), groups of rows, the text that helps under a field, radio buttons and the text area. The fields themselves are the ones on the Inputs page; nothing here changes their border, size or states.

Mobile considerations

The label goes above its field and the dots go away; switches stay on their row. Fields, options and buttons get 44px touch targets.

Phone < 576pxTablet 576–991pxDesktop ≥ 992px

Toasters & Alerts

How the product talks back. Toasts float for a moment after an action (saved, sent). Alerts sit inside the page and stay until the problem is solved. The Error alert is the red alert for errors from the server. Progress shows how far a long task has gone. Click the × on a toast to dismiss it; Reset brings them back.


        

        

        
Mobile considerations
There is no top-right on a phone: toasts span the width at the top.

Layout & Navigation

        
Structural components that organize content within a page: collapsible sections, the tabs used on detail screens and on the Standard Grid (and how they become a dropdown on mobile), a metric card, and the user chip with its profile menu.


        

          
Accordion

          
A collapsible section with a chevron that rotates and a "Show Less" text link — the active section gets an indigo border so it's clear which one the user is editing.

          

        


        

          
Section tabs (in a section header)

          
On detail screens (Customers, Styles…), any section with 2 or more sub-sections shows them as a tab bar in its own header, so people go straight to the part they need. It is the only tab style used inside sections, and it is used instead of a side menu. Try each case below.

          

        



        

          
Tabs on mobile · dropdown

          
Below 768px both kinds of tabs become one dropdown with the current tab as its value. Six or eight tabs wrapped in rows would take half the screen before any content; the dropdown takes one line. The demos above switch on their own at that width; this is the same thing drawn at 390px.

          

        


        

          
Standard Grid view tabs

          
Only on the Standard Grid: each saved view is a tab in a gray bar flush with the top of the grid panel. The active tab is white, joins the panel and carries an indigo line; the close × shows on the active tab and on hover.

          

        


        

          
Keyboard focus

          
What happens when someone works without the mouse. The clip shows the left side menu, the header and the Standard Grid used only with the keyboard; the key pressed appears bottom right. Every interactive element can be reached with Tab and shows the focus ring.

          

            
            

              
KeyWhat it does

              
Tab / Shift + TabNext / previous element, in the order you read the screen: menu, header, then the page from top to bottom, left to right.

              
EnterActivates buttons, links and tabs; opens or closes a menu section, a dropdown or a panel.

              
SpaceChecks a checkbox or a radio; also activates buttons.

              
EscCloses the open dropdown, panel, flyout, tooltip or dialog and puts focus back on what opened it.

              
↑ ↓Move through the options of an open select or menu.

            

            
    
              
  • Ring: 2px #321FDB, 2px away from the element; on dark rows (menu levels 2–4, open level 1) a white 2px ring inside the row (−4px). Inputs use their own focus (border + 3.5px halo).
    • 
              
  • Keyboard only: the ring appears with the keyboard (:focus-visible), never on mouse click.
    • 
              
  • Never hidden: no outline:none without a replacement; nothing that can be clicked is out of the Tab order.
    • 
              
  • Focus stays put: when a list re-renders (opening a menu section, switching a tab) focus stays on the same element; when a panel closes it returns to its trigger.
    • 
              
  • Tooltips open on focus too, so icon-only buttons are named for keyboard users.
    • 
              
  • Skip to Content is the first Tab stop on every page (see Accessibility & Content).
    •

A label and a large value — for KPI summaries above a grid.

Logos here are generic placeholders — real third-party marks aren't reproduced in this reference doc.

Page Structures

        
Three structures cover almost every screen in the product. Reach for one of these before inventing a new layout — each one is a live, working reference, not a screenshot.


        

          
1. Standard Grid

          
The default list/search screen: saved-view tabs, a toolbar, a sortable table and the footer pills. Toolbar order is fixed: Filter · Cols & Sort · Views · Export · Refresh · More, six buttons maximum, More always at the far right; every extra action goes inside More. Icon-only on desktop; text next to the icon on mobile and tablet. Rows: hover #F0EFFC, selected #E4E1F7 + 3px bar; the checkbox column stays pinned and the ID column is at least 190px wide.

          

            

          

        


        

          
2. Edit Grid

          
The detail/edit screen for a single record: a header with status and actions, a collapsible section, a two-column field grid with dotted leader lines connecting label to control, and a meta footer.

          

            

          

        


        

          
3. Print Grid

          
The print/export preview: a dark toolbar for page navigation, zoom and rotation, over a white, print-styled document with a meta table and an itemized grid (labels in Title Case, text in #000 / #404040).

Accessibility & Content

        
Interaction, accessibility, and voice rules already agreed on for every feature.


        

          
Accessibility & interaction

          

            
    
              
  • Focus (:focus-visible, keyboard only): 2px #321FDB ring with a 2px offset around the whole control. On dark surfaces (the active menu item) the ring turns white with a -4px offset, because indigo on the blue menu measures 1.28:1.
    • 
              
  • Skip to content is the first focusable element of every screen: hidden until the first Tab, Enter jumps straight to the content (demo below).
    • 
              
  • Errors: red border #C91741 + a red message under the field that says how to fix it, no icon. The message is tied to the field with aria-describedby and aria-invalid="true"; after a failed submit, focus moves to the first invalid field.
    • 
              
  • Required fields carry a red "*" after the label and aria-required="true".
    • 
              
  • Labels are visible and tied to their control (label for / aria-labelledby); a placeholder is never the only name.
    • 
              
  • Color is never the only signal: a selected row has a checkbox and a 3px bar; information has the ⓘ icon; errors have a message.
    • 
              
  • Tooltips open on hover and on keyboard focus; icon-only buttons also carry an aria-label.
    • 
              
  • Loading: buttons that wait for the server keep their size, show a spinner and can't be pressed twice (aria-busy="true").
    • 
              
  • prefers-reduced-motion is respected — transitions drop to 1ms if requested.
    • 
              
  • Full-name tooltips appear in collapsed mode; in expanded mode, only when the label is truncated.
    • 
              
  • Opening a flyout explicitly hides any tooltip left over from a previous hover.
    • 
              
  • Single-open accordion per level (opening one item closes its siblings).
    • 
              
  • Only one header dropdown open at a time; closes on outside click or Escape.
    • 
            

          

        


        

          
Skip to content

          
Click inside the frame, then press Tab: the link appears; press Enter and focus jumps to the content, skipping the menu.

          

        


        

          
Copy voice & tone

          

            
    
              
  • Casing: names in Title Case, sentences in sentence case (see the text rules on the Typography page).
    • 
              
  • Buttons start with a verb and say the action ("Discard", "Keep Editing", "Add Sort Column"); never "Yes" / "No".
    • 
              
  • Dialog titles state the decision ("Discard changes?"), never a generic "Alert".
    • 
              
  • Direct and warm, no "please."
    • 
              
  • Distinguishes an empty-field error from an invalid-format error.
    • 
              
  • Contextual messages — e.g. "That email doesn't look right — check for typos."
    • 
              
  • Password policy follows NIST SP 800-63B: 10-character minimum, strength meter, no forced composition rules.
    • 
              
  • All visible/accessible text is in English (aria-labels included) — the product serves a U.S.-based customer base.
    •
